# p0_databricks_workspace (Resource)

A Databricks workspace installation. P0 calls the workspace at `workspace_url` as its account's service principal.

**Important:** Before creating this resource, the workspace's account must be installed (see the `p0_databricks_account` resource), and its service principal must be assigned to the workspace as `USER`, or as `ADMIN` when `is_workspace_admin_enabled` is `true`. Assign it with `databricks_mws_permission_assignment` or `databricks_permission_assignment`.

A workspace that P0 hasn't finished installing, such as one imported before its install check passed, plans an update, and applying it finishes the install.

**Note:** This integration is currently in beta.

For the full install steps, see [Installing Databricks](https://docs.p0.dev/integrations/resource-integrations/databricks/installation).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Adds a workspace in an installed Databricks account, by assigning the
# account's service principal to it: as a workspace user, or as a workspace
# admin if local.enable_workspace_admin is true. Apply it as a Databricks
# account admin, once per workspace. Then add the workspace's catalogs (see
# p0_databricks_catalog).
#
# To install the connector, account, workspaces and catalogs in one
# configuration that wires them together, see
# https://registry.terraform.io/providers/p0-security/p0/latest/docs/guides/databricks

terraform {
  required_providers {
    databricks = {
      source  = "databricks/databricks"
      version = ">= 1.115.0"
    }
    p0 = {
      source = "p0-security/p0"
    }
  }
}

locals {
  databricks_account_id = "01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef"
  workspace_id          = "1234567890123456"
  # If this configuration also holds the workspace's databricks_mws_workspaces,
  # pass its workspace_id, workspace_url and workspace_name straight through.
  workspace_url = "https://dbc-1234abcd-5678.cloud.databricks.com"
  # The workspace's name in P0. Requests show it, and approval rules can match
  # it.
  workspace_name = "analytics-prod"

  # Whether users can request workspace admin on this workspace. P0's service
  # principal is a workspace admin only while this is true. P0 refuses to
  # turn it off while an approved workspace-admin request here hasn't ended.
  enable_workspace_admin = false
}

# Workspace assignments are made at the account level, so the provider must be
# account-level. Unless told how to sign in, it uses whatever Databricks
# credentials it finds, such as a CLI login, so everyone who plans or applies
# needs their own account admin login. To avoid that, sign it in as a service
# principal with the account_admin role and a federation policy, which needs no
# secret: add auth_type = "env-oidc" and client_id = "<its application ID>", and
# set DATABRICKS_OIDC_TOKEN to an identity token that the policy accepts.
provider "databricks" {
  host       = "https://accounts.cloud.databricks.com"
  account_id = local.databricks_account_id
}

# The service principal of the account's p0_databricks_account, found by its
# application_id. If this configuration also holds the account, as P0's
# installer arranges it, refer to its databricks_service_principal instead.
data "databricks_service_principal" "p0" {
  application_id = "8c5e2e0a-8f0d-4a3e-9d61-3b2f4c7a1e05"
}

# USER is enough for Unity Catalog grants. Only workspace-admin requests need
# ADMIN, which P0 checks when is_workspace_admin_enabled turns on.
resource "databricks_mws_permission_assignment" "p0" {
  workspace_id = local.workspace_id
  principal_id = data.databricks_service_principal.p0.id
  permissions  = [local.enable_workspace_admin ? "ADMIN" : "USER"]
}

resource "p0_databricks_workspace" "example" {
  id                         = local.workspace_id
  account                    = local.databricks_account_id
  workspace_url              = local.workspace_url
  workspace_name             = local.workspace_name
  is_workspace_admin_enabled = local.enable_workspace_admin
  depends_on                 = [databricks_mws_permission_assignment.p0]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `account` (String) The `id` of the `p0_databricks_account` that this workspace is in
- `id` (String) The Databricks workspace ID
- `workspace_name` (String) A name for the workspace in P0, e.g. `analytics-prod`. Requests show it, and approval rules can match it with the workspace filter's name key. Changing it updates the workspace in place. A configuration that holds the workspace's `databricks_mws_workspaces` can pass its `workspace_name` here.
- `workspace_url` (String) The workspace's URL, e.g. `https://dbc-1234abcd-5678.cloud.databricks.com`: `https://` and a lowercase host on the workspace domain of the account's cloud, with no port, path or trailing slash. P0 calls the workspace there, and checks that it belongs to this workspace ID. P0 can't change a workspace's URL, so a new value replaces the workspace. A configuration that holds the workspace's `databricks_mws_workspaces` can pass its `workspace_url` here.

### Optional

- `is_workspace_admin_enabled` (Boolean) Whether users can request workspace admin on this workspace. Defaults to `false`. The service principal needs an `ADMIN` assignment, in place of `USER`, only when this is `true`, and P0 then checks that it is a workspace admin. Changing it updates the workspace in place. P0 needs the role to revoke the workspace admin it granted, so it refuses to turn this off while an approved workspace-admin request on this workspace hasn't ended. Its error starts `P0 still manages workspace admin on Databricks workspace` and lists those requests. Let them end, or revoke them, then apply again. If P0's check fails or P0 refuses, the apply fails, and the workspace stays as it was. Terraform may change the assignment in that apply before P0 refuses, so if it did, apply your previous configuration again to restore `ADMIN`.

### Read-Only

- `state` (String) This item's install progress in the P0 application:
	- 'stage': The item has been staged for installation
	- 'configure': The item is available to be added to P0, and may be configured
	- 'installed': The item is fully installed
